title: Develop customer attestation templates and run pricing sensitivity experiment for enterprise security add-ons
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: produce a lightweight, modular set of customer security attestations (SIG/CAIQ aligned) and run a small pricing sensitivity experiment that ties enterprise security artifacts to optional contract SKUs.

Scope:
- Author a one-page attestation summary for sales and a full SIG/CAIQ answer pack mapped to Redwood controls.
- Create a short template (PDF + editable doc) customers can sign to acknowledge attestation receipt.
- Produce a matrix that maps each SIG/CAIQ claim to internal control owners, evidence artifacts (logs, architecture diagrams, contract clauses), and whether it is included in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Design and execute a controlled pricing experiment with 6 pilot enterprise prospects to evaluate willingness-to-pay for a security-attestation add-on vs. bundled SLAs.

Why now: enterprise prospects frequently request attestations during procurement. Current ad-hoc responses slow sales and create scope creep in commercial terms. Packaging a repeatable attestation product will speed procurement and let us measure direct revenue impact of selling security as a discrete add-on.

Deliverables:
- Attestation one-pager (PDF) + editable Google Doc (customer-facing).
- SIG/CAIQ answer pack (CSV & markdown) with per-claim mapping to evidence.
- Internal playbook for SEs and SalesOps describing how to request, deliver, and log attestations.
- Pricing experiment plan and data collection template.
- Experiment results readout with recommendation (bundle vs add-on, suggested price bands).

Out of scope for this ticket: full legal negotiation of contract language, creation of new legal terms. Those will be handled by Legal in follow-up if experiment indicates a new SKU is warranted.
acceptance_criteria: Customer-facing one-pager and editable doc available in Drive and linked from sales playbook
SIG/CAIQ answer pack produced and reviewed by Security (SOC/Platform) with correctness sign-off
Evidence matrix completed with owners for each claim and accessible to Customer Success
Pricing experiment executed with at least 4 completed prospect interactions and data captured in the provided template
Experiment readout with a clear go/no-go recommendation and proposed next steps for Legal and RevOps
comments: 2026-02-19 - Asha Kapoor: Kickoff meeting with Security, Legal, and SalesOps. Agreed to keep initial attestation doc lightweight (2 pages) and iterate based on pilot feedback.
2026-02-25 - Marcus Liu: Drafted initial SIG/CAIQ mapping. Left open questions for ENG-4125 about evidence extraction for KV cache encryption logs.
2026-03-02 - Tori Mendes (Security): Reviewed answers and suggested we standardize wording for 'data residency' and 'third-party audits' to avoid ambiguity.
2026-03-05 - Legal (via comment): We can provide attestation but cannot commit to specific contractual audit cadence in a template. Recommended addendum route if customer requests recurring audits.

2026-03-09 - Marcus Liu: Pricing experiment plan sent to Sales pilot cohort. Plan includes A/B: (A) attestation as free with 12-mo committed Dedicated, (B) attestation as $5k one-time add-on. Tracking sheet shared.

2026-03-12 - Asha Kapoor: Progress update - 3 pilot prospects engaged, 1 completed purchase with attachment of attestation, early signal that some prospects prefer included in bundle. Next update after experiment completes (target 2026-03-22).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: making the attestation too broad reduces legal defensibility; making it too narrow reduces sales usefulness. Decided to keep factual controls and point to evidence rather than promising auditability. Sales prefers included bundles for ease of close; Finance wants a measurable add-on experiment first.
